cases.proposed_rule: Demote boundaries that end immediately before a clause's main predicate or nominal head; only rank them highly when the head (verb/noun phrase that completes the assertion) is already present earlier in the piece.

summary: The prompt is ranking a risky boundary too highly when it cuts off before a clause's main head (priority error), producing mistranslations under tight budgets. Other boundaries cut at topics, subordinate clauses or quote openings and are harmless; the remedy is to demote boundaries that end immediately before a predicate/nominal head while allowing (higher rank) breaks at self-contained topical NPs, subordinate clauses that don't assert reversible facts, and quotation openings.
